diagnoses.description: The skill lists redaction “patterns” like email wildcards (`*@*.edu`), arXiv IDs (`arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX`), and DOI formats (`10.XXXX/...`), but the provided PyMuPDF implementation uses `page.search_for(pattern)` which only finds exact literal substrings (no wildcard/regex support). This will systematically miss real emails/IDs/DOIs unless the caller enumerates every exact string beforehand, undermining anonymization.

The skill hard-codes a policy to stop redacting at the first page whose text contains the substring “references”. This heuristic is brittle (the word “references” can appear in running text or headings earlier), potentially causing redaction to stop too early and leave author-identifying info unredacted on later pages.

The skill instructs redacting only “Before References” / skipping the References section entirely. For anonymization, identity leaks can appear after references (appendices, author contribution/bio sections, repeated footers/headers, camera-ready/accepted statements, etc.). This restriction can cause missed leaks and conflicts with the task’s requirement to redact all authorship-revealing information.

The skill provides no procedure for sanitizing PDF metadata/XMP (Author/Creator/Producer/Keywords/etc.) or for removing/redacting link annotations that can embed deanonymizing URLs (e.g., arXiv links, personal webpages). This is a common leakage channel for anonymization tasks and is not addressed in the skill guidance or example code.

The “CRITICAL RULES” require verifying that 80%+ of original text remains, but the provided `verify_redaction` enforces only a 70% retention threshold. This internal inconsistency can allow over-redaction to pass verification contrary to the skill’s stated requirements.
